artworks.title: Saturn Devouring His Son
artworks.description: One of Goya's Black Paintings, executed directly on the walls of his house outside Madrid and later transferred to canvas. It shows the Titan with nightmarish intensity, devouring one of his children to forestall the prophecy that a son would overthrow him. Now in the Museo del Prado, it has become the defining modern image of Cronus.

artworks.title: Saturn Devouring His Son
artworks.description: A Baroque oil painting commissioned for the Torre de la Parada, the Spanish royal hunting lodge. Rubens depicts Saturn tearing into his infant son beneath his scythe, rendering the myth with visceral naturalism. The work hangs in the Museo del Prado in Madrid and anticipates Goya's later treatment of the same subject.

artworks.title: The Mutilation of Uranus by Saturn
artworks.description: An oil-on-panel ceiling painting from the Sala degli Elementi of the Palazzo Vecchio in Florence. It depicts the pivotal act of divine succession in Hesiod's Theogony: Cronus castrating his father Uranus, the sky, with the adamantine sickle.

films.title: Wrath of the Titans
films.description: The Clash sequel makes Kronos the lava Titan breaking Tartarus — Cronus as the imprisoned father whose sons must stop him from reclaiming the world.

popCulture.title: Percy Jackson & the Olympians
popCulture.creator: Rick Riordan
popCulture.description: Riordan's series casts Kronos as the rising Titan lord — the swallowed-children myth rewritten as a demigod war against Time's king.

popCulture.title: The Last Olympian
popCulture.creator: Rick Riordan
popCulture.description: The series climax brings Kronos into Luke's body for the siege of Olympus — Cronus as the final boss of a children's epic.

popCulture.title: God of War III
popCulture.creator: Santa Monica Studio
popCulture.description: Kratos climbs and kills the colossal Titan Cronos in the desert of the lost — the child-swallower as a boss the size of a mountain.

popCulture.title: Saturday
popCulture.description: English Saturday descends from Latin dies Saturni — Cronus' Roman name still naming the seventh day of the week.

popCulture.title: Saturnalia
popCulture.description: Rome's midwinter festival of gift-giving and role-reversal honored Saturn — Cronus' Latin face as the Golden Age returned for a week.
